answer: Multi-anchor distance bounding deters Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to unique coordinates via speed-of-light radio timing. When an agent sells data from a willow wetland, karst cave, or meadow plot, nearby anchors measure signed round-trip latencies to triangulate its radio and reject colocated clones. Attackers incur the hardware and siting cost of physically separated radios per identity. However, colluding anchors can falsify timestamps to validate duplicate nodes.
